text:
Maya: quick question — for console saved queries we currently attach scope: route OR global. UX asks: should we default a saved query created from a route view to be route-scoped or try to infer/merge model filters? Seeing a bunch of confusion in support tickets.

Sam: route-scoped by default feels most intuitive. if i'm saving while on a route page i expect "this route view" to be what I get back. :+1:

Jon: agree on expectation, but routes often include model filters implicitly (users pick model on the route page). if the model filter doesn't survive when someone opens the saved view from the model page that causes surprising diffs in telemetry & cost numbers.

Alisha: exactly — telemetry shows tokens & latency per (route,model). If savedQuery drops model filter depending on context, rerun numbers differ. We should preserve the exact filter set somewhere in the saved object.

Maya: concrete example: click Save on /routes/checkout with filters: `model=redwood-7b`, `time=7d`, `stat=latency`. If scope=route only, users later open it from model view and see different token totals.

Sam: proposal sketch: have savedQuery keep full filterSet + a default_scope field. shape example (conceptual):
```
{"filters": [{"k":"model","v":"redwood-7b"}, {"k":"time","v":"7d"}], "default_scope":"route", "origin":"/routes/checkout"}
```
This lets the UI decide what to apply depending on entry point.

Jon: that's ok but api consumers (and share links) need a clear contract. i'd rather a small, explicit schema: `scope` and `scopedFilters` e.g. `scopedFilters: {route:[...], model:[...], org:[...]}` — then we avoid surprises when opening from another context.

Alisha: +1 to keeping telemetry parity: add an optional `telemetry_baseline_checksum` when saved so console can show "numbers may differ" if metric drift detected. We can compute a cheap hash of the query fingerprint and sample windows.

Maya: UX question: if someone from model page opens a route-saved-view that includes model filters, should we open it in the source scope (route) with a small banner, or open using the current page context but warn that some filters were dropped? My vote: open in source scope and show banner "This view was saved from Route /checkout — showing route-scoped filters. [Open anyway in model view]"

Sam: banner + explicit CTA is good. fallback behavior: apply only compatible filters automatically and show a toast listing omitted filters ("model filter omitted").

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: feature/telemetry-saved-query-api -> canary in staging @ 1800 UTC :rocket:

Jon: action items: I'll draft the API PR (savedQuery schema + examples) and add migration notes for older saved queries.

Sam: I'll mock the banner copy + share-link param (e.g. `?saved=123&scope=route`) and drop into product board.

Alisha: I'll spec telemetry checksum and edgecases for long windows.

Maya: +1. also request small RFC so infra teams know the new shape. Sam — can you create rfc/saved-query-scope.md?

Sam: yep, will do today.

Maya: thanks all — moving to backlog grooming. :memo:
